verdict: This one makes me lean forward, and for the right reason: the 3D is not a skin, it is the must-have, and every pixel that moves (heat ramp, path polyline, floor heat, ghost vs solid counters) is a direct readout of the same headless simulate() the eval script runs on real November 2011 invoices. The three must-haves of 4.2 are met literally (JSON with top-100/pick counts/orders; grid racks + aisles + dock + animated picker walking the aisle graph with live counters; swap-and-replay with a fast-movers-nearest-dock baseline), all three watch-outs are honoured explicitly (C-invoices and non-product codes removed with counts shown, aisle-graph walking proven by the overlay, instancing with a quality tier), and the held-out time split plus README drift test is more rigour than any other 4.2 team will bring. I verified tonight that the HF parquet mirror answers 200 with 7,156,732 bytes and that every pinned package (three 0.186.1, R3F 9.8.2, drei 10.7.9, postprocessing 6.39.5 with peer three <0.187, camera-controls 3.1.2, zustand 5.0.15, motion 14.5.0, vite 8.3.5, tailwind 4.3.3) is the current npm latest with peers satisfied, so the demo-safety story is real. What stops it from being a 9 or 10 is overreach: the scripted ghost race compares Baseline against Baseline-plus-one-swap, which will show two pickers walking identical routes for most orders; the 5-minute script carries about eleven interactions and will run seven; the headline comparison leans on a StockCode-ascending "original" that is a straw man; the AI-opponent story depends on an SA-vs-ABC gain that in single-order TSP picking is typically a few percent and shrinks on held-out, which must be measured before it is promised; and the technical surface (Held-Karp, NN+2-opt+Or-opt, S-shape, return, SA with incremental delta cache and subsample, worker protocol, instanced lerps, post-FX tiers, SVG map, drift tests) is more than two sleep-deprived humans can explain line by line after a two-hour read-through, which rule 3 of the instructions makes an explicit gate. Cut the surface by a third, race Original against Player/SA, measure the SA gap tonight, and this is a top-three entry among thirty.
fatal_flaws: Explainability gate: instructions section 3 says every team member must be able to explain the submitted solution including AI-generated code; the plan has roughly 24 agent-hours of TypeScript (five routing policies, SA with incremental delta evaluation plus SKU->orders index plus 600-order subsample plus milestone re-evaluation, worker protocol, instanced fly-lerps, post-FX quality tiers, zustand store, SVG slot map, drift tests) reviewed in one 07:30-09:30 window by humans who slept six hours. The first Q&A question will target the most impressive claim (SA delta cache) and a fumbled answer there taints every number on the KPI card. Must be fixed by cutting scope and by humans owning and annotating a sim folder small enough to whiteboard.

The scripted WOW 2 is self-defeating: ghost = Baseline, solid = Baseline + one swap. With exact per-order routing and short orders (median 2-5 top-100 stops), both pickers walk pixel-identical routes on most of the 8 replayed orders and the two counters do not diverge; a tired judge sees two pickers walking together and concludes the game does nothing. Must race Original (or the player's pre-edit starting layout, which must be Original) against Player or SA, on pre-selected deterministic orders where the routes visibly differ.

The 5-minute script will not fit: camera flight + hottest-box click + Data panel (25 s allotted), play + routing toggle + simulate twice, baseline fly + drag + 8-order race at 20x (about 8 orders x 3-4 s of walking = 25-35 s before narration), 8 s live SA, evidence panel + README screenshot, stretch demo, team slide. That is roughly 7 minutes delivered by a nervous human. Overrunning the demo window is the single most common way strong entries lose; the script must be cut to three beats before rehearsal, not after.
weaknesses: Straw-man 'original': StockCode-ascending row-major is effectively a random layout (top sellers 85123A, 22423, 85099B, 84879, 47566, 20725 are scattered across the code range). Original->Baseline will show a large saving (likely 30-45% walking distance) that proves nothing about the player or the optimiser. If the KPI headline or deck says 'X% saved vs original', an expert judge calls it out. The headline must be Player/SA vs Baseline on held-out; Original is context only.

Expected effect sizes are small where it matters: in single-order picking with optimal or S-shape routing, ABC/COI slotting captures most of the gain and affinity-based slotting adds low single-digit percent in the literature; held-out will be smaller still. 'Pick time' dilutes further because 8 s x lines is layout-invariant (a 4-line order carries 32 s handling against perhaps 60-100 s walking). A tired judge reading 'SA beats baseline by 1.8% held-out' shrugs unless the pitch pre-frames it as 'ABC takes most, affinity takes the residual, here is how much survives held-out'. None of this is measured yet; the script quotes placeholders Y% and Z%.

Live SA in 8 s is likely to show a flat-ish objective curve: a move involving a top SKU re-routes 300-400 orders (85123A alone appears in several hundred Nov 2011 invoices), so even with the 600-order subsample the budget is perhaps 1-3k accepted/rejected moves over 112! permutations. The shipped 60 s offline result is the real number; the live run must be framed as a visual, not the score, or precomputed longer (10 min in Node) with the log committed.

Mild leakage: the fast-mover baseline ranking (and ideally the top-100 catalogue) must be computed from opt-set pick counts only, otherwise the baseline has seen held-out orders. Also, the KPI card showing held-out numbers live during editing lets a player overfit the held-out set; held-out should appear on 'Submit to leaderboard'. Neither is fatal but both are exactly what a rigour-minded judge probes after the honesty pitch.

Orders with more than 12 distinct nodes are routed heuristically and counted, but their share of total distance is not reported; wholesale invoices with 15-25 top-100 lines traverse almost every aisle regardless of slotting and dominate total metres, which both caps slotting gains and makes 'count of heuristic orders' an incomplete disclosure. Report share of distance, not just count.

drei DragControls wraps Object3D children; it does not drag instances of an InstancedMesh. Dragging a box would need a proxy mesh plus instanceId raycast, which is fiddly on a trackpad on stage. The must-have says 'swaps or drags', so click-to-swap alone satisfies it; DragControls is 1-2 h of risk for no scoring value.

frameloop='demand' with CameraControls, growing Line points, instance lerps and motion counters needs invalidate() plumbing in every animated path; a missed invalidate shows as a frozen picker on stage. With under 50 draw calls, frameloop='always' with a dpr cap is simpler and cannot freeze.

Bloom + SMAA at dpr 1.5 on a 1080p projector means 2880x1620 render targets plus mip chain; on a UHD 620-class iGPU that drops below 30 fps and the auto-tier probe may pass at load (empty scene) then fail during the race. Default post-FX off on the demo laptop; the ghost at 0.35 opacity and the emissive pulse read fine without Bloom.

Plan contradiction: 'Integration + QA (humans + one agent) 03:30-05:00' while humans sleep 01:30-07:30. Overnight integration is agent-only and needs an unattended push token; say so in the plan, and keep commits small and hourly rather than hourly squashes of agent output (the commit-history review in instructions section 3 looks for cadence, not bulk).

Exact-duplicate-row removal is moot because picks are distinct (Invoice, StockCode) pairs; keep the count in meta but do not spend narration on it. Conversely, the coverage number (top-100 share of order lines, likely 15-25% in Nov 2011) is the number a judge will fixate on; it must be on the first Data panel screen, not buried.
Two UIs (3D plus a full SVG slot map with affinity hints) double the polish surface. The 2D map is justified as the phone fallback and the share-link viewer; affinity hints are the optional part.
Determinism double-click and the README screenshot are demo seconds spent proving things judges already assume; both belong on Q&A cards, not in the 5 minutes.
fixes: Cut the sim surface to what two humans can whiteboard: Held-Karp (bitmask DP, <=12 nodes) + nearest-neighbour+2-opt fallback (flagged) + S-shape as the single heuristic ablation; drop Or-opt and the return policy. SA: keep the SKU->orders index (a swap re-scores only orders containing either SKU) but compute each affected order's distance by calling route() directly on a fixed opt-set subsample; no cached-delta bookkeeping beyond that, and a vitest property test that the incremental score equals a full recompute. Target src/sim under 600 lines with doc comments; humans annotate it by hand at 07:30 and write the Q&A cards themselves.

Rewrite the demo to three beats: (1) 0:00-1:15 data -> twin: QR slide, camera flight, click hottest box, Data panel with stage counts and coverage %, press Play on one invoice, counters tick, say 'walks aisles only'. (2) 1:15-3:00 the race: one click 'Baseline' (boxes fly, KPI updates), one scripted swap chosen in rehearsal that measurably helps, then 'Replay Race' with ghost on ORIGINAL and solid on PLAYER over 6 pre-selected high-contrast orders (about 20 s), KPI card shows Original / Baseline / Player on opt and held-out. (3) 3:00-4:20 the opponent and the evidence: 'Run optimiser' with the objective curve, result flies in, leaderboard, Evidence panel with opt vs held-out side by side and the routing ablation line; 4:20-5:00 limitations spoken + team slide. Routing toggle, determinism, README screenshot, share-link phone, stretch goals go to Q&A cards.

Make the headline comparison Player and SA vs Baseline on held-out orders (16-30 Nov 2011); show Original only as a grey reference row and label it 'declared convention, effectively random'. Consider seeded-random as the Original so no judge can allege a convenient convention.

Run prep.py and the full eval tonight before any deck text is written: get real numbers for Original/Baseline/SA on opt and held-out, coverage %, orders count, median stops, share of distance in >12-stop orders, SA in-sample vs held-out gap. If SA held-out gain is under about 2%, reframe the narrative as 'ABC captures most of the gain; here is the measured residual and how much of it survives held-out' and make the honesty the hook rather than the magnitude.

Compute the fast-mover baseline ranking from opt-set pick counts only; state that the top-100 catalogue uses the whole month as the forward-pick zone definition. Show held-out numbers on 'Submit to leaderboard' rather than live while editing.
Report share of total distance (not just count) from heuristically routed orders in the Evidence panel; add walking-time share of pick time so the 8 s handling constant is transparent.
Drop DragControls; click-to-swap (click box A, click box B or an empty slot) in both 3D and the 2D map, with a highlighted selection and a 0.8 s fly animation, is the entire interaction.

Use frameloop='always' with dpr capped at min(devicePixelRatio, 1.5); ship post-FX behind a feature flag defaulting OFF on the demo laptop; enable only if the pre-flight probe shows >=55 fps during an actual race, not at load.

Precompute the SA layout offline for 10 minutes in Node with seed and log committed (public/layouts/sa_seed42.json plus the objective trace); the live 8 s run is a 'watch it work' visual whose result is shown next to, not instead of, the shipped number.

Reserve one hour of art direction before 09:00 (rack palette, floor grid lines, dock glow, light fog, picker silhouette, HUD typography at >=18 px) because the failure mode of this idea is a grey-box scene with a cyan line; the ghost race only lands if the scene already looks finished.
Fix the plan text: overnight integration is agent-only with an unattended push token; humans' 07:30-09:30 window is read-through plus the end-to-end demo on the venue-class laptop, not integration.
Pre-select the race invoices deterministically (store their ids in a config) so the race is identical in rehearsal, on stage, and in the recording.
steal_worthy: Ghost replay: a semi-transparent copy of the agent executing the before-state on the identical input, side by side with the after-state, with two counters diverging live; it is the most legible 'measured not claimed' device in the whole set and transfers to 3.2 (uncontrolled vs scheduled load), 4.3 (pre-event vs re-planned routes) and 4.1 (fixed vs markdown policy).

Drift test: npm run eval writes results.md with commit hash and timestamp, and a vitest test fails if the committed file differs from a fresh run, so README, app and deck cannot disagree; cheap and judges remember it.

In-app Data panel that shows the preprocessing meta verbatim (rows at each cleaning stage, coverage %, split sizes, generated_at, script sha) and makes each 3D object clickable back to its source record; this answers the data-provenance question before it is asked.
Time-based held-out split shown on screen with the optimiser restricted to the first half, and the in-sample vs held-out gap printed rather than hidden.
Routing-policy ablation (exact DP vs S-shape vs nearest-neighbour) on the same layout as a one-line sensitivity check that converts a 'why that assumption' question into a chart.

Quality-tier FPS probe with a 2D fallback mode and a share-by-URL hash of the state, so the judge can open the same state on a phone; zero-backend, zero-secret architecture with three identical static mirrors plus local vite preview.

The 'declared assumptions' panel that lists every synthetic design choice (geometry, speeds, handling time, original-layout convention) next to the real-data facts, so the honest-limitations slide is already in the product.
